question: Where is Morgan Stanley investing in technology for its advisors?

claims.text: On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the firm had been investing over multiple years "in all of our processes and our systems" to have a robust infrastructure to grow. She tied this to technology, to better understanding its data, and to servicing clients better.

On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CEO Ted Pick said the financial advisor sees an integrated firm offering "unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology" and fair compensation. He also said the firm is investing in E*TRADE. The CFO described advisors sending "next best actions" to retail clients, and said the self-directed technology handled high volumes without interruption.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), the CFO said early AI use cases, some live and some in pilot, are showing progress. One is LeadIQ, which she called an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with financial advisors. She also named DevGen AI (developer efficiency) and Parable (data analysis and summaries), which are not described as advisor-facing. Pick said the mantra is to invest in technologies, some efficiency-driven and some effectiveness-driven.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), a company representative said LeadIQ helps introduce advisors to clients interested in advice and uses AI. The representative said technology on both the revenue and expense sides should help drive margin.

On the same 4Q25 call (January 2026), Pick said the firm is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are "difficult for others to replicate". He listed alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending. He also said growth plans embed increasing adoption of AI tools across the enterprise and the client base.

The 2025 10-K (published February 2026) says the Wealth Management segment's ability to compete across advisor-led, workplace and digital direct channels is affected by multiple factors. One of them is "our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization."

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), Pick said Morgan Stanley has built advantages on a platform of a self-directed channel, a workplace offering and advisor-client relationships. He said these advantages preserve the firm's moat and "make technology a differentiator in our favor."

gaps.what: Dollar amounts or budget share for advisor-specific technology spend, and a full list of advisor-platform tools, are not found in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley investor day or Wealth Management presentations, and the earnings financial supplement or technology disclosures
